children: are higher in choppy premarket trading as Wall Street digests the pet retailer’s mixed second-quarter results and improved full-year outlook against a meaningful decline in the company’s liquidity.
With an increased customer base (up 3.8% year-over-year to 21.7M), Chewy’s

sales and profits for the quarter improved by 7.4% and 9%, respectively. The increase did little to bolster the company’s profit margin, however, as the cost of sales increased by nearly the same as net sales, keeping the company’s gross margin unchanged and net margin improving by just 40 basis points to 2.4%. Excluding certain items, adjusted EBITDA margin expanded by 90 basis points to 6.8%.
The customer metrics were mixed as well, with a 3.8% increase in active customers, slightly better than estimates, but with net sales per active customer increasing by a less-than-expected 2%.
On the balance sheet, however, free cash flow declined by 15.5% to $89.5M, while cash and cash equivalents experienced a 29% decline to $611M.
expects sales to be within a range of $3.32B to $3.36B, straddling the $3.33B consensus estimate.
raised its sales outlook to a range of $13.46B and $13.57B from $13.40B to $13.55B with a $13.515B midpoint that beats the $13.48B estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA margin range was narrowed to 6.7% to 6.8% from 6.6% to 6.8% previously.

title: Chewy's raised outlook gives shares a lift despite falling liquidity
